observations.pairA_difference: Very subtle: D6B1 has a faint soft shadow/glow bleeding onto the grey desktop around the card's left, right and bottom edges (the grey darkens gradually near the corners, e.g. from RGB 92 down to ~86), plus a faint 1-2px light highlight running along the very top edge of the card (top row ~33,33,33 fading to the panel's base 18,18,18 by the 3rd row). 72E4 has neither: the grey stays flat 92,92,92 right up to the card edge with no bleed, and the top edge is a flat dark line with no highlight. This is a pixel-level difference (checked by diffing the two images), not something obvious at a casual glance.
observations.pairB_difference: Same difference as pair A, same magnitude and pattern: A83F has the soft edge shadow/glow bleeding into the grey background plus the faint top-edge highlight line; 5C09 is flat with neither effect.
observations.position_same: yes - confirmed both images in each pair are identical pixel dimensions and the pixel-diff bounding box matches the card's own boundary (not shifted), so the surface sits at the same position and size in both.
observations.content_lost: no - visually both images in each pair show identical text and elements (title, fields, buttons for pair A; title, checklist rows, source chips, footer links for pair B); the only measured pixel differences are the edge shadow/highlight described above plus negligible anti-aliasing noise, not missing content.

why.pairA: 72E4 has no drop-shadow/glow at the card's edges (the flat grey desktop touches the card directly, no bleed) and no top-edge highlight, so it reads as fused into the screen; D6B1 adds a faint shadow bleeding onto the desktop plus a top rim-light, which are elevation/separation cues that make it read more like a distinct floating panel sitting over the desktop.
why.pairB: Same reasoning as pair A: 5C09 is flat with no edge shadow or top highlight, reading as part of the screen's top edge; A83F's added soft shadow and top rim-light give it a slight elevated, separate-window feel.
